quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop completely as soon as possible.
Stop and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and continue carefully. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crosswalk is ahead.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers about schools. It tells you to slow down, be careful, and look for children.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into your lane after passing a car?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to move back.
When you look over your shoulder and see the other car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You have enough space to move back when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror. This means there is a safe distance between you.

questions.question: What should you do if oncoming headlights are blinding you at night?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look at the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This helps you stay on the road safely.

questions.question: The road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. The broken line is next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles here.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass. Just make sure no oncoming cars are coming.

questions.question: How should you make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb.
Start in the right lane, then move toward the middle before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning. Slow down and move to the right lane as close as possible to the curb before you turn right.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive at this speed through the intersection.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
You cannot drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed allowed. You can drive slower if conditions require it, but you cannot drive faster.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
Carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means do not pass. A broken yellow line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you about the road ahead?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road curves right, then left.
The road curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a reverse curve. The road will curve to the right first, then to the left.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: If you come to a complete stop first.
If you wait until the light changes.
If you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
questions.explanation: You can proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane and the way is clear. This is true even if other signals are showing at the same time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming up so you can prepare for traffic or prepare to turn.

questions.question: Where can you safely pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.
Wherever signs and pavement markings allow passing.
In a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and pavement markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, curves, or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and pavement markings permit it and when you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: If you come to a complete stop first.
If you wait until the light changes.
If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. Before turning, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: For any turn, use the lane closest to the direction you want to travel. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances are longer and crashes are more severe when vehicles travel faster.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the posted speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid puddles and other slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, and oil. Dry, solid surfaces are the safest for driving.

questions.question: You must use your low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off wet conditions and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can be cited.

questions.question: On a road with a broken white centerline, you:

options.text: Must stay in your lane.
May cross the centerline to change lanes.
May change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean traffic moves in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings when they follow traffic signals. If there is no traffic signal, you must stop for pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

questions.question: What is the thinking of defensive drivers?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting possible mistakes from other drivers and being prepared to handle them.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction they must drive. You must obey the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: The light is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter until you can drive all the way across.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter until you can drive all the way across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely through it before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speed increases the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speed means you need more following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the risk of death in a crash increases. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is unlikely. Higher speeds also require longer stopping distances, so increase your following distance when you speed up.

questions.question: A DUI conviction is based on a blood alcohol concentration of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
50 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent is always illegal in Tennessee. Drivers under 21 can be charged with a BAC as low as 0.02 percent. You can be convicted of DUI even with a BAC below the legal limit.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should:

options.text: Stop, listen, and move forward carefully.
Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Whenever you approach a place where people may cross your path or where traffic meets, look left and right to make sure nothing is coming.
